parts.text:
The bones of the human head make up the **skull** (which is divided into the neurocranium/braincase and the facial skeleton) as well as the **associated bones** of the middle ear and throat. 

In total, there are **29 bones** in the head and neck area. Here is a complete breakdown of these bones, organized by their location and function.

---

### 1. The Cranial Bones (Neurocranium) – 8 Bones
These bones fuse together to form the protective "braincase" that houses and protects the brain.

*   **Frontal Bone (1):** Forms the forehead and the upper part of the eye sockets (orbits).
*   **Parietal Bones (2):** A pair of large, curved bones that form the upper sides and roof of the skull.
*   **Temporal Bones (2):** A pair of bones located on the lower sides of the skull (around the temples) that house the structures of the inner ear.
*   **Occipital Bone (1):** Forms the back and base of the skull. It contains the *foramen magnum*, a large opening through which the spinal cord connects to the brain.
*   **Sphenoid Bone (1):** A complex, butterfly-shaped bone that sits in the middle of the skull base. It connects almost all other cranial bones.
*   **Ethmoid Bone (1):** A light, spongy bone located at the roof of the nose, separating the nasal cavity from the brain.

---

### 2. The Facial Bones (Viscerocranium) – 14 Bones
These bones form the structure of the face, protect sensory organs (eyes, nose, mouth), and provide attachment points for facial muscles.

*   **Mandible (1):** The lower jawbone. It is the strongest, largest, and **only movable** bone of the skull (excluding the tiny bones in the ears).
*   **Maxillae (2):** The two bones that fuse to form the upper jaw, holding the upper teeth and forming part of the nose and eye sockets.
*   **Zygomatic Bones (2):** Commonly known as the cheekbones. They form the cheeks and parts of the outer eye sockets.
*   **Nasal Bones (2):** Two small, oblong bones that meet in the middle to form the bridge of the nose.
*   **Lacrimal Bones (2):** The smallest and most fragile bones of the face, located in the inner corner of each eye socket. They contain the tear ducts.
*   **Palatine Bones (2):** L-shaped bones located at the back of the nasal cavity that form the back part of the hard palate (roof of the mouth).
*   **Inferior Nasal Conchae (2):** Thin, scroll-like bones located inside the nasal cavity that help filter and warm inhaled air.
*   **Vomer (1):** A thin, flat bone that forms the lower part of the nasal septum (the divider between your nostrils).

---

### 3. The Auditory Ossicles (Middle Ear Bones) – 6 Bones
Located inside the temporal bones of the skull, these are the smallest bones in the human body. There are three in each ear, and they vibrate to transmit sound waves to the inner ear.

*   **Malleus / Hammer (2)**
*   **Incus / Anvil (2)**
*   **Stapes / Stirrup (2)** *(Note: The stapes is the smallest bone in the entire human body).*

---

### 4. The Hyoid Bone – 1 Bone
*   **Hyoid Bone (1):** A U-shaped bone located in the front of the neck, just below the mandible. While not technically part of the skull, it is grouped with the bones of the head. It is unique because it **does not articulate (connect) with any other bone**; instead, it is suspended by muscles and ligaments and supports the tongue and swallowing movements.

---

| | Parietal | 2 | Paired |

| | Ethmoid | 1 | Unpaired |
| **Face (14)** | Mandible | 1 | Unpaired |
| | Maxilla | 2 | Paired |
| | Zygomatic | 2 | Paired |
| | Nasal | 2 | Paired |
| | Lacrimal | 2 | Paired |
| | Palatine | 2 | Paired |
| | Inferior Nasal Conchae | 2 | Paired |
| | Vomer | 1 | Unpaired |
| **Ears (6)** | Malleus, Incus, Stapes | 6 | 3 pairs |
| **Neck (1)** | Hyoid | 1 | Unpaired |
